html:
SMTO-PSM-0024 — The server address isn't valid

GUID: 9f180bb6-96e5-4e34-925f-51eb9f3ebe39
Slug: typed-parameter-host-invalid
Domain: PSM · Subsystem: psm

What happened

  • The server address field holds something SMTO can't use as an address, like a full web link or a name with spaces. Nothing was saved or connected.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Change the server or host to just the name or number, for example server1.example.com or 192.168.1.20. Do this on the parameter's Value tab, or in your /discoverdb command. This field takes only the server's address; the connection type and port are stored separately.
  2. Remove anything like https://, a slash and path, a :port ending, or spaces. Put the port in the port field instead. Those extra parts make the address invalid for this field.
  3. For a long address with many colons (IPv6), wrap it in one pair of square brackets, like [2001:db8::1], then select Save. SMTO needs the brackets to tell that kind of address apart from a port.

What success looks like

  • Parameter Store shows Saved and the parameter appears in the list.

If it still fails

  • Ask the person who manages the server for its exact name or address, then try again. If it still fails, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Server-host validation rejected the value: it is missing, contains a URL scheme, path, spaces or invalid hostname labels, or has malformed IPv6 brackets.

What this means

  • Server-host validation rejects malformed IPv6 brackets, invalid IP/hostname labels, missing host or URL-like discovery syntax. Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.

Why this can happen

  • Server-host validation rejects malformed IPv6 brackets, invalid IP/hostname labels, missing host or URL-like discovery syntax.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the host component separately from scheme, port, path and credentials.

How to fix it

  • Enter only a hostname or IP address in the server/host field: no 'https://', path, port suffix or spaces, labels of 1-63 characters not starting or ending with '-', and IPv6 in one pair of brackets like [2001:db8::1]. Validated by validate_typed (src/agent_runtime/parameters/templates.py) for server_connection profiles and by _validate_database_discovery_request (discoverdb.py) for /discoverdb.
  • Use a hostname or IP address without a URL scheme or path; use correct brackets for IPv6.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended hostname or IP passes its profile/discovery host rules.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
